entryAnswer.explanation:
What the adapter does. `mountSpendingAlertsDisplay` takes the caller's already-created `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback and delegates to the example-local binding `mountSpendingView` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-view-binding.ts:17-20), which subscribes to the five ports `assessment, publication, coverage, issues, startup` (causal-view-binding.ts:14) and publishes `{ values, unavailable }` (causal-view-binding.ts:25-31). The adapter adds no runtime: it never calls `spendingAlertsFor(...).compose(...)` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-entry.ts:49-76) and never supplies input facts; the view is the frozen five-port object built by the preset (examples/spending-alerts/causal-preset.ts:171-177, type at 206). `toSpendingDisplay` is a pure projection: a port present in `observation.values` is rendered as its current value, and a port absent from it is rendered as `available: false` and listed in `unavailable` (causal-view-binding.ts:29). The README's ordinary-panel row describes exactly this contract: "five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup" (examples/spending-alerts/README.md:34), and the ordinary panel is the consumer precedent (examples/spending-alerts/causal-ordinary-panel.ts:5-18).

What "a value becoming unavailable" means. The binding deletes a port's entry when the port emits `INVALIDATE` or `ERROR` (causal-view-binding.ts:42-44). At the substrate level `INVALIDATE` clears the node's cache to SENTINEL, sets `hasData = false`, runs the invalidate hooks and broadcasts `INVALIDATE` downstream (packages/ts/src/node/node-output-runtime.ts:451-459); a dep-side `INVALIDATE` also drops the cached latest view and cascades (packages/ts/src/node/node-input-runtime.ts:43-78). So "unavailable" means there is no current usable fact on that port right now — the old displayed value must not be retained (README.md:138). It is not a statement that the run ended, that the instance stopped, or that a request failed: startup "started" does not prove authorization or completion (README.md:139), a flagged assessment still needs evidence and permission (README.md:140), and a publication success covers only that exact request (README.md:141). The five latest values are also not an atomic multi-port snapshot (causal-view-binding.ts:10, README.md:142).

What unmounting means. The returned cleanup is the binding's `stop` (causal-view-binding.ts:32-36, returned at 51): it unsubscribes every port subscription in reverse order and is idempotent via the `closed` flag. Unsubscribing removes the sink from the node's subscriber set and deactivates the node when the last subscriber leaves (packages/ts/src/node/node.ts:441-444); the binding's own doc says the returned function "ends observation only. Run ownership stays with the application" (causal-view-binding.ts:16). Per README.md:143, "Panel detach: observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations." The demo shows this: after `detachPanel()` the render count stops changing while `app.inspect().inFlight` is still 1 and the record has no outcome (examples/spending-alerts/causal-graded-demo.ts:146-148, 170-172), the write completes while detached (causal-graded-demo.ts:182-188), and reconnecting the same original view renders again without a second write (causal-graded-demo.ts:189-192). Cleanup is therefore not recovery: unknown or reconciliation-required outcomes must be preserved by the application, not treated as resolved by panel cleanup (README.md:146-151), and the protocol has no END message — business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination are distinct (README.md:153-157).

Scope discipline. The adapter only reads the original view; it does not touch capabilities, the owning Graph, diagnostics or retained evidence, consistent with "Display components receive only the original `.view`" (README.md:91-96). It also does not use the public `subscribeNodeValues` adapter, which ignores INVALIDATE and is not a substitute for this view contract (README.md:159-161). No code was executed; this is a static adapter over the supplied sources.
